lines.japanese: 眠れない…
lines.english: I can’t sleep.

lines.japanese:
時計の秒針が何度も周回するのを、
さっきからぼうっと眺めている。
lines.english: I’ve been staring blankly at the second hand going around and around.

lines.japanese:
…実際には、長針でさえ何回か周回してたけど、
それでも今の俺に、眠気は降りてこない。
lines.english: The minute hand has made a few circuits of its own, in fact, and still sleep refuses to come.
“Ngh…”

lines.japanese: かずさは、とっくに眠ってくれた。
lines.english: Kazusa fell asleep ages ago.

lines.japanese:
ちょっとばかりテンション高かったけど、
今日からは、俺を風呂場から追い出し、
食事だって、自分の手で食べた。
lines.english: She was a little overexcited, but as of today she was throwing me out of the bathroom and even feeding herself again.

lines.japanese:
ベッドに潜ってからも、しばらくは俺に対する恨み節や、
追加公演のことや日本を去った後のことを
つらつら話してたけど…
lines.english: After crawling into bed, she spent a while cataloging her grievances against me, talking about the encore concert, and wondering aloud what would happen after she left Japan…

lines.japanese:
すぐに外出の疲れと喋り疲れが重なって、
俺の目の前で無防備に、柔らかな寝息を立て始めた。
lines.english: Before long, the strain of going out and talking so much caught up with her. Right in front of me, utterly unguarded, she began to breathe softly in her sleep.

lines.japanese:
だから俺は、今日こそ安心して、
深い眠りに落ちてもいいはずなのに…
lines.english: So tonight, of all nights, I ought to be able to relax and sink into a deep sleep myself…
“Nnnnngh!”

lines.japanese: なのに、記憶が邪魔をする。
lines.english: But my memory won’t let me.

lines.japanese:
この期に及んで、更に大きな爆弾を落としてくれた、
冬馬曜子という人の残した言葉が…
lines.english: Youko Touma’s words—an even bigger bomb, dropped at the worst possible moment…
“…Excuse me?”

lines.japanese:
「だから、白血病。
普通は薄幸のヒロインがかかる病気なんだけど、
神様も何を勘違いしたのかしらね」
lines.english: “I said leukemia. It’s normally the sort of disease they give some tragic young heroine. God must have gotten his casting mixed up.”

lines.japanese:
行方をくらました曜子さんを無理やり探し出し、
こうして直接会いに来たのは、
もちろん、かずさのことを話すためだった。
lines.english: I had hunted down Youko after she disappeared and insisted on meeting her for one reason: to talk about Kazusa.

lines.japanese:
俺がもう、かずさを支えられなくなってしまったことを
正直に告げて、助けを仰ぐため…
lines.english: I had come to admit that I could no longer support Kazusa—and to ask Youko for help.

lines.japanese:
そして、今までさんざん俺たちを振り回した責任を
取ってもらうためだった。
lines.english: I had also come to make Youko answer for the way she had spent all this time jerking the two of us around.

lines.japanese:
「半年前くらいかな…
たった二時間のコンサートで、
体がふらつくようになってきたのよ」
lines.english: “It started about six months ago, I suppose. A two-hour concert was suddenly enough to leave me unsteady on my feet.”

lines.japanese:
責任、取ってもらうはずだったのに。
これで、かずさも救われるはずだったのに…
lines.english: She was supposed to take responsibility. This was supposed to save Kazusa…

lines.japanese:
「三、四曲目あたりで動悸や息切れが激しくなってきて、
終わったあとも一時間くらい治まってくれなくてね」
lines.english: “By the third or fourth piece, my heart would be racing and I could hardly breathe. Even after the performance, it took a good hour to settle down.”

lines.japanese:
曜子さんは、まったく予想もしていなかった場所に
俺を呼び出した。
lines.english: Youko had summoned me to the last place I would ever have expected.

lines.japanese: 峰城大学病院…
lines.english: Houjou University Hospital.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、とうとう来たか糖尿病って思ってたんだけど」
lines.english: “I assumed the diabetes had finally caught up with me.”

lines.japanese:
「…普通は誰でもそう思います。
親子とももっと節制すべきです」
lines.english: “That would be the obvious conclusion. You and your daughter could both stand to exercise a little more restraint.”

lines.japanese:
「あはは、ギター君は相変わらずだ。
わたしに対しても、いっつも偉そうなんだから」
lines.english: “Ha! You haven’t changed, Guitar Boy. Even with me, you always talk as if you’re in charge.”

lines.japanese:
「………すいません。
まだ、状況飲み込めてなくて」
lines.english: “I’m… sorry. I still haven’t quite taken this in.”

lines.japanese:
「…ま、そうよね。
当の本人でさえ、受け入れるのに結構時間かかったし」
lines.english: “No, I suppose you wouldn’t have. It took me long enough, and I’m the one who has it.”

lines.japanese: うちから歩いて１５分…
lines.english: Only a fifteen-minute walk from my apartment…

lines.japanese:
七年間通った峰城学園の敷地内にある、
総合病院の個室のベッドに、その体を横たえていた。
lines.english: She lay in a private room at the general hospital on the Houjou campus, where I had spent seven years of my life.

lines.japanese:
「向こうの病院で軽く診てもらった時には、
貧血だって言われたから、それから必死で食べて。
…ワインも白をやめて赤に替えたしね」
lines.english: “The first doctor I saw over there said it was anemia, so I started eating for dear life. I even gave up white wine and switched to red.”

lines.japanese: 「それ、色だけじゃ…」
lines.english: “That only changes the color…”

lines.japanese:
「それでもやっぱり症状が改善しなくてね。
一年前ならオールナイトで弾いても平気だったのに」
lines.english: “Strangely enough, I didn’t improve. Only a year ago, I could play all night without a problem.”

lines.japanese:
逆にそっちの方がおかしいって話もあるけど。
…かずさが高い壁だと強く意識するほどに。
lines.english: Though arguably that was the abnormal part. It only drove home how formidable a wall Kazusa still had to climb.

lines.japanese:
「それで、これはヤバいんじゃないのってことになって、
日本で信用のおける高柳先生に診てもらうことにした」
lines.english: “Eventually I decided this might actually be serious, so I came back to Japan and put myself in the hands of Dr. Takayanagi. He’s someone I trust.”
lines.japaneseRuby:
「それで、これはヤバいんじゃないのってことになって、
[R日本^こっち]で信用のおける高柳先生に診てもらうことにした」

lines.japanese:
高柳憲正教授なら知ってる。
俺が大学にいた頃から医学部長だった。
lines.english: I knew Professor Norimasa Takayanagi. He had already been dean of the medical school when I was at the university.

lines.japanese:
「その手の病気に関しては
世界的権威って言われてるし、
何よりまぁ昔から色々とあった間柄だし…」
lines.english: “He’s considered one of the world’s leading authorities on this sort of illness. More importantly, he and I have… quite a history.”

lines.japanese:
そして、またしても意外なところから
かずさの父親候補が…
lines.english: And from yet another unexpected quarter emerged a new candidate for Kazusa’s father…

lines.japanese:
「来日してから何度か検査入院して、
だいたい病気の正体も掴めてきて…」
lines.english: “I was admitted for tests several times after coming to Japan. By then, they had more or less worked out what was wrong…”

lines.japanese: 「入院…」
lines.english: “Admitted…?”

lines.japanese:
つまり、来日中に何度も行方をくらましてたのは、
古い友人に会うためとか、
朝まで飲み明かすためとかじゃなくて…
lines.english: So all those times she vanished during her visit, it hadn’t been to see old friends or drink until dawn…

lines.japanese:
「さてどうしようかって時に、
結構ヤバい症状が来ちゃってね。
…それが、かずさのコンサートの夜」
lines.english: “We were just deciding what to do when I had a particularly nasty episode. That was the night of Kazusa’s concert.”

lines.japanese: 「あの日から…？」
lines.english: “You’ve been here since that night…?”

lines.japanese: 「二日ほど記憶がないんだけどね」
lines.english: “I don’t remember the next two days.”
“Ngh…”

lines.japanese:
かずさが、誰も支えてくれる人がいなくて
悲嘆に暮れていたとき…
lines.english: While Kazusa had been drowning in grief with no one there to hold her up…

lines.japanese:
それ以上に、
娘の差し出す手を必要としてる人がいたなんて。
lines.english: someone else had needed her daughter’s outstretched hand even more.

lines.japanese:
「ま、今は大丈夫。
週明けには退院できるから」
lines.english: “I’m all right now. They’ll let me out early next week.”

lines.japanese: 「かずさにはそのこと…」
lines.english: “Does Kazusa know…?”

lines.japanese:
「言えると思う？
今のあの子に」
lines.english: “Do you honestly think I could? The way she is now?”

lines.japanese: 俺は今日、この人を責めるつもりだった。
lines.english: I had come here today intending to condemn this woman.

lines.japanese:
自分のことを棚に上げ、説教の一つでもかますつもりで
気合いを入れていた。
lines.english: I had steeled myself to set my own failings aside and give her a piece of my mind.

lines.japanese:
それなのに…
どんだけ何もわかってなかったんだよ、俺。
lines.english: And yet… How could I have understood so little?

lines.japanese: 「もしかして、かずさの来日公演も…？」
lines.english: “Was this why you arranged Kazusa’s concerts in Japan?”

lines.japanese:
「いつかは連れてくるつもりだったけど、
急いだのはこのためね」
lines.english: “I always meant to bring her eventually. This is why I hurried.”

lines.japanese:
今回の来日公演は、
単に、売り時を見逃さない冷静なプロデューサーとしての
判断から、だけじゃなかった。
lines.english: The tour had not been merely the coolheaded calculation of a producer determined to strike while her artist was marketable.

lines.japanese:
「冬馬かずさは、日本で受け入れられるのか。
ウチのバカ娘は、もう一度日本で暮らせるのか。
その両方を、確かめたかったの」
lines.english: “Could Kazusa Touma win acceptance in Japan? Could my idiot daughter live here again? I wanted an answer to both.”

lines.japanese: 娘の将来を見届けられるかどうかわからない…
lines.english: She could no longer be sure she would live to see her daughter’s future…

lines.japanese:
けれどそれを娘に伝えられない母親の、
悩んだ末の、ショック療法。
lines.english: Yet she could not tell Kazusa that. This was the desperate shock treatment a mother had settled on after agonizing over it.

lines.japanese: 「…わたしが生きてるうちにね」
lines.english: “…While I’m still alive.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな…」
lines.english: “You can’t mean…”

lines.japanese:
彼女のしたことは、今のところ見事に失敗してるけど、
事情を知ってしまった今、
もう、その親馬鹿を責めることは、俺には…
lines.english: So far, her plan had failed spectacularly. But now that I knew why, I could no longer bring myself to blame a mother for loving her daughter too much…

lines.japanese:
「言っておくけど、
すぐ死ぬつもりなんか全然ないわよ？」
lines.english: “For the record, I have absolutely no intention of dying anytime soon.”

lines.japanese: 「…はい」
lines.english: “…Good.”

lines.japanese:
「最近はだいぶこの病気の致死率も下がってきてるし、
薬打ちまくって、金使いまくって、
少なくとも１００までは生き延びるわよ？」
lines.english: “The mortality rate has fallen considerably. I’ll pump myself full of drugs, pour money into treatment, and live to a hundred at the very least.”

lines.japanese: 「お願い、します」
lines.english: “Please do.”

lines.japanese:
そうやって、まだ言葉の端々に、
冬馬曜子ならではの強さが見られることもあるけれど…
lines.english: Now and then, that unmistakable Youko Touma strength still flashed at the edges of her words.

lines.japanese:
「ただね………もう、ウィーンには戻らない。
わたしはもう、日本を離れるつもりはないの」
lines.english: “But… I’m not going back to Vienna. I’ll never leave Japan again.”

lines.japanese: 「っ…曜子さん」
lines.english: “…Youko.”

lines.japanese:
それでも今の彼女に、
かつて意気揚々と日本を捨てたお気楽な開拓者の面影は、
もう、見られなかった。
lines.english: Even so, nothing remained in her now of the carefree pioneer who had once abandoned Japan in triumph.

lines.japanese:
「自分の生まれた国ですもの。
何だかんだ言って、世界で一番愛してる国ですもの」
lines.english: “It is the country where I was born. For all my complaints, it’s still the country I love most in the world.”

lines.japanese:
その決断を責めることはできないし、
同じ日本人としてはシンパシーを感じられる思いだし、
事情を知れば知るほど、反対する理由が消えていく。
lines.english: I could not fault that decision. As another Japanese person, I could even understand it. The more I learned, the fewer reasons I had to oppose her.

lines.japanese: けれど…
lines.english: But…

lines.japanese: 「かずさは…？」
lines.english: “What about Kazusa?”

lines.japanese: 「………どうしよっか？　ギター君」
lines.english: “…What do you think we should do, Guitar Boy?”

lines.japanese: 「そんな…っ」
lines.english: “You can’t…”

lines.japanese:
ちょっと冗談混じりな口調だったけど、
彼女のその言葉は、
きっと嘘偽りのない嘆息だったんだと思う。
lines.english: There was a trace of humor in her voice, but I think the words themselves were an entirely honest sigh.

lines.japanese:
「今のかずさは…
曜子さんを超えることだけが人生の目標で、
なのに曜子さんしか頼れる人がいなくて…」
lines.english: “All Kazusa lives for now is surpassing you. And yet you’re the only person she has to depend on…”

lines.japanese:
そして多分かずさは、
日本に、なんの未練もなくなってしまっていて…
lines.english: And Kazusa probably no longer had anything left to tie her to Japan…

lines.japanese:
「そっか…
かずさのこと、拒絶したのね、あなた」
lines.english: “I see… You rejected her.”
“Ngh…”

lines.japanese:
「ねぇ、あの子のどこが駄目だったの？
そりゃピアノ以外に取り柄ないし、暗いし、ワガママだし、
意地っ張りで諦めの悪さはちょっと退くレベルだけど…」
lines.english: “What was wrong with her? Fine, the piano is the only thing she’s good at. She’s gloomy, selfish, stubborn, and so incapable of giving up that it’s honestly disturbing, but…”

lines.japanese:
「そういう問題じゃ…ないです。
あいつに不満なんかありません」
lines.english: “That isn’t the problem. I have no complaints about her.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなこと平気で言える人間、
世界であなたしかいないから期待してたんだけどなぁ」
lines.english: “You’re the only person alive who could say that with a straight face. I had such high hopes for you.”

lines.japanese: お互い、相手に期待しすぎてた。
lines.english: We had both expected too much of the other.

lines.japanese:
「また負けたか、我が娘は…
しかも五年前と同じ相手に」
lines.english: “Defeated again, my daughter—and by the same opponent as five years ago.”

lines.japanese: 「やめて…ください」
lines.english: “Please… stop.”

lines.japanese: この人なら、かずさを…
lines.english: I had simply assumed that if anyone could help Kazusa…

lines.japanese:
あの気難しい天才にして社会不適合者を、
なんとかしてくれるんじゃないかって、勝手に…
lines.english: if anyone could manage that temperamental genius and social catastrophe, it would be this woman.

lines.japanese: 「こっちとしても賭けだったのよね…」
lines.english: “It was a gamble for me too.”

lines.japanese:
「わたしだって、一応親なんだし、
かずさが独り立ちできるまで
一緒にいてやりたいって思ってる」
lines.english: “I am her mother, after all. I want to stay beside Kazusa until she can stand on her own.”

lines.japanese: けれど、そのことを責められるわけなんかない。
lines.english: But I had no right to blame her for that.

lines.japanese:
「けれどもう、
それをウィーンで実現させることはできない。
ワガママではあるけれど、自分の一生のことだから」
lines.english: “But I can no longer do it in Vienna. Selfish or not, this is my one life.”

lines.japanese:
だってお互い、自分の一生を守るために、
相手に期待したってことでは一致してる。
lines.english: In that sense we were alike: we had each placed our hopes in the other to safeguard our own futures.

lines.japanese:
「だから、かずさを無理やり日本に連れてきた。
…永住、するために」
lines.english: “That is why I dragged Kazusa to Japan. I meant for us to settle here permanently.”

lines.japanese:
それは、素直な気持ちで受け止めれば、
俺にとって、心の底から喜ばしいことのはずだった。
lines.english: If I could have accepted that news without all the complications surrounding it, I should have been genuinely happy.

lines.japanese:
「ピアノの方に限って言えば、
今の日本なら、今のかずさなら、
もう、ヨーロッパじゃなくてもやっていける」
lines.english: “As far as her career goes, Japan is ready for Kazusa now—and Kazusa is ready for Japan. She no longer needs Europe.”

lines.japanese:
五年前、あんな悲しい別れ方をしたかずさが、
二度と会えないかもしれないって思っていたかずさが、
これからは、いつでも会える距離にいる。
lines.english: Kazusa, from whom I had parted so painfully five years ago—Kazusa, whom I had thought I might never see again—would henceforth live close enough to meet whenever I wished.

lines.japanese:
「もともとフリューゲルの爺さんは今年で引退だし、
次の師匠も日本で見つけてある」
lines.english: “Old Flügel is retiring this year anyway, and I’ve already found her next teacher in Japan.”

lines.japanese:
「…橋本健二っていう若手ナンバー１ピアニストを育てた、
フランス人のおばちゃんでね。
…まぁ昔は男取り合ってよく大喧嘩したけど」
lines.english: “A Frenchwoman who trained Kenji Hashimoto, the brightest young pianist in the country. We did have some spectacular fights over a man once, but that was years ago.”

lines.japanese:
お互いや、仲間たちの記念日に…
それどころか、単に思い立っただけでも、
すぐに集まれるメンバーの中にかずさがいる。
lines.english: Kazusa would be among the people who could gather at a moment’s notice—for our own special occasions, for our friends’, or simply because one of us felt like it.

lines.japanese:
「だから後は、かずさが再びここで暮らせるか、
それだけが、一番の心配事だった」
lines.english: “My only real concern was whether Kazusa could live here again.”

lines.japanese:
かずさと、俺と…
そして雪菜の、“あの三人”を、
いつでも再現できる。
lines.english: Kazusa, me… and Setsuna. We could put “those three” back together whenever we wanted.

lines.japanese:
「…でも結局、駄目だったみたいね。
かずさを吹っ切れさせることも、
かずさの思いを遂げさせることも」
lines.english: “But apparently it didn’t work. I couldn’t help Kazusa put you behind her, and I couldn’t help her win you either.”

lines.japanese: また、三人でいられる。
lines.english: The three of us could be together again.

lines.japanese:
けれどそれは、五年前に温泉宿で、
永遠の友情を誓い合った三人ではなくて。
lines.english: But we would not be the three who had sworn eternal friendship at that hot-spring inn five years ago.

lines.japanese:
誰もが誰かのことを、
もう、友達だなんて思えない三人で…
lines.english: We would be three people, none of whom could still think of both of the others as friends…

lines.japanese:
「あなたこそが、
かずさを日本に戻すための最後の希望で…
そして最大のネックだった」
lines.english: “You were my last hope of bringing Kazusa back to Japan—and the greatest obstacle in her way.”

lines.japanese:
「俺にそんなこと言われても…
いきなりそんなこと言われても…」
lines.english: “What am I supposed to do with that? You can’t just tell me this out of nowhere…”

lines.japanese:
「あの子の気持ち、聞いたんでしょ？
それで受け入れなかったのよね？
…なら、それが結果なんだからしょうがない」
lines.english: “She told you how she felt, didn’t she? And you chose not to accept her. That is the outcome, and we’ll simply have to live with it.”

lines.japanese:
「っ…受け入れられると思いますか？
五年間、音信不通だったんですよ？
どうやって信じろって言うんです！？」
lines.english: “How could I accept it? She hadn’t said a word to me in five years! How was I supposed to believe her?”

lines.japanese:
「ずっと一緒にいたわたしが保証しましょうか？
あの子が五年間、どれだけ色ボケてたか。
…会えもしない、たった一人の男相手に」
lines.english: “Would you like a guarantee from the woman who spent those five years beside her? I could tell you precisely how hopelessly lovesick she was over the one man she couldn’t even see.”

lines.japanese: 「っ…別に、そんな」
lines.english: “That doesn’t mean…”

lines.japanese:
「あの子は毎日十時間、あなたと会話してたのよ。
だから、想いが色褪せることなんかあるはずなかった」
lines.english: “Kazusa spoke to you ten hours every day. Her feelings never had the slightest chance to fade.”

lines.japanese: 「十時間…」
lines.english: “Ten hours…”

lines.japanese: それは、かずさが毎日ピアノと語らう時間。
lines.english: Ten hours. That was how long Kazusa spent speaking through the piano every day.

lines.japanese:
親に反抗していた時期を除いて、
そして…俺に悪態をついていた日を除いて。
lines.english: Except while she was rebelling against her mother—and on those days when she had me there to curse at instead.

lines.japanese:
「そうやって、ずっと冷めない恋をしてたから、
あの子のピアノは、どんどん色っぽくなってって、
いつの間にか、世界に認められるようになっちゃって…」
lines.english: “Her love never cooled, and it made her playing more and more sensual. Before anyone knew it, the world had come to recognize her…”

lines.japanese: 「そんな、そんな…」
lines.english: “No… that can’t…”

lines.japanese:
「かずさの告白、聞いたんでしょ？
なら今さら、信じられないなんて言うのはナシよ？」
lines.english: “You heard Kazusa’s confession. It’s far too late to claim you can’t believe her now.”

lines.japanese:
幼稚な感性だからこそ。
視野が狭すぎるからこそ。
lines.english: Because her feelings were so childish. Because her world was so narrow.

lines.japanese:
他になにも興味を持たなかったからこそ、
かずさのピアノは、あんなに輝いたって…
lines.english: Because she had cared for nothing else, Kazusa’s piano had come to shine as brilliantly as it did…

lines.japanese: やっぱり芸術って………馬鹿みたいだ。
lines.english: Art really was… stupid.

lines.japanese:
「でもねぇ…相手が悪かった。
かずさにとって、あまりに高嶺の花だった」
lines.english: “Still, she chose the wrong man. You were far too unattainable for her.”

lines.japanese:
「俺が…高嶺の花？
どうして？」
lines.english: “Me? Unattainable? Why?”

lines.japanese:
「だってギター君、普通の人だもの。
そんなハードルの高い相手、
やっぱりあの子には無理だったのよ」
lines.english: “Because you’re an ordinary person, Guitar Boy. Of course Kazusa could never clear a hurdle that high.”

lines.japanese: 「意味が…わかりません」
lines.english: “I don’t understand.”

lines.japanese:
「だってわたしたちは、
普通の人の人生を壊す力を持ってしまっている。
しかも、それを抑えることができないの」
lines.english: “People like us have the power to destroy an ordinary person’s life. Worse, we cannot rein that power in.”
“Ah…”

lines.japanese:
「だから、もしもあの子が、
あなたを手に入れようとしたら、
あなたの周囲の世界ごとぶち壊すことになる」
lines.english: “If Kazusa tried to make you hers, she would shatter the entire world around you.”

lines.japanese:
日本にとどまらない、世界規模での演奏活動。
その才能と生活を維持するための膨大なコスト。
ここ数日の、本人すら望んでいない周囲の喧騒。
lines.english: A career spanning the globe, not merely Japan. The staggering expense required to sustain her talent and her way of life. The uproar of the past few days, which even Kazusa herself had never wanted.

lines.japanese:
生活の規模も、人生の目的も、
幸せの基準さえも、何もかもが違う、俺たち。
lines.english: The scale and purpose of our lives, even the standards by which we measured happiness—nothing about us was the same.

lines.japanese:
俺には、一生縁のない、
馴染めるはずのない、世界…
lines.english: It was a world I would never touch, a world I could never belong in…

lines.japanese:
「それは、別のある人にとっては、
とても残酷で、無情で、本当に酷いこと」
lines.english: “And for someone else, that would be a cruel, merciless, truly terrible thing.”

lines.japanese:
そして、もしリスクを覚悟で飛び込んだとしても、
その時、普通の俺の側にいようとしてくれていた人は…
lines.english: Even if I accepted the risk and plunged into Kazusa’s world, what would happen to the person who had tried to remain at the side of ordinary, unremarkable me…?

lines.japanese: 雪菜の、幸せは…
lines.english: What would become of Setsuna’s happiness?

lines.japanese: やっぱり、考えるまでもない。
lines.english: There was no need to think about it after all.

lines.japanese:
かずさが好きになったのは、本物の俺じゃない。
かずさが勝手に作り上げた理想像に過ぎない。
lines.english: Kazusa had not fallen in love with the real me. She loved an ideal she had fashioned for herself.

lines.japanese:
だって雪菜はこの５年間、
ずっと本物の俺に振り回されてきた。
lines.english: Setsuna, meanwhile, had spent the last five years being dragged around by the real me.

lines.japanese:
理想と現実のギャップに苦しみ、対話を繰り返して、
やっと今の俺たちになったんだ。
lines.english: She had suffered through the gulf between dream and reality, and she had kept talking to me until at last we became what we were now.

lines.japanese:
だから、雪菜の想いこそが…
俺と雪菜の語らいの上に築かれた関係こそが真実で。
lines.english: That was why Setsuna’s feelings were real—why the relationship Setsuna and I had built through all those conversations was the truth.

lines.japanese: 「曜子さん、俺」
lines.english: “Youko, I…”

lines.japanese:
曜子さんが、どれだけかずさを庇っても、
かずさの想いがどれだけ純粋で本物でも。
lines.english: No matter how fiercely Youko defended Kazusa, no matter how pure or genuine Kazusa’s feelings might be…

lines.japanese:
いや、だからこそ、
答えは明確に、俺の目の前に転がっている。
lines.english: No—precisely because Kazusa’s feelings were real, the answer lay right in front of me, clear and inescapable.

lines.japanese:
雪菜を選ぶことこそが、
俺にとって何の間違いもない、満点の答えなんだって。
lines.english: Choosing Setsuna was the perfect answer, the one answer that could not possibly be wrong.

lines.japanese: だから、言わないと。
lines.english: I had to say it.

lines.japanese: 俺には、雪菜しかいないって。
lines.english: Setsuna was the only one for me.

lines.japanese: はっきりと、かずさに別れを告げるしかないんだって。
lines.english: I had no choice but to tell Kazusa, clearly and finally, that it was over.

lines.japanese:
「だからね、ギター君。
こうなってしまった以上、
あなたは、あの子を思い切り振ってあげて」
lines.english: “So listen, Guitar Boy. Now that things have come to this, you need to reject her completely.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「せめて、少しでも傷の治りが早くなるように、
すぱっと切り捨ててあげて」
lines.english: “Make a clean cut. At least give the wound a chance to heal quickly.”

lines.japanese:
そこまでわかっていながら、
またしても俺は失敗した。
lines.english: I knew exactly what I had to do, and still I failed again.

lines.japanese:
「絶対に、自分で傷を癒そうなんて考えないこと。
あなたが少しでも隙を見せたら、
あの子は絶対に諦めないわよ？」
lines.english: “And never imagine that you can help her recover yourself. Show her the slightest opening and she will never give up on you.”

lines.japanese:
心の中で決心したことを、
結局、いつまでも口に出すことができなかった。
lines.english: In the end, I could not bring myself to speak the decision I had reached in my own heart.

lines.japanese: 「そんな…」
lines.english: “But…”

lines.japanese:
「そんなことあるわけないって思う？
…それこそ、普通の人の感覚ね」
lines.english: “You think that could never happen? That is exactly how an ordinary person would think.”

lines.japanese:
おかげでいつの間にか、また立場は元に戻り、
俺は、かずさを庇う側に回ってしまう。
lines.english: And just like that, our positions had reversed again, leaving me back where I started: defending Kazusa.

lines.japanese:
「かずさはね、本質的には、わたしと同じ色情狂なの。
一般人並の理性なんて持ち合わせてないの」
lines.english: “Deep down, Kazusa is just as much of a sex fiend as I am. She doesn’t have an ordinary person’s capacity for restraint.”

lines.japanese: 「よ、曜子さん」
lines.english: “Y-Youko…”

lines.japanese: また、曜子さんに逆に追い込まれてしまう。
lines.english: Once again, Youko had maneuvered me into a corner instead.

lines.japanese:
「でなければ、五年も会わずにいた男を
ひたすら想い続ける訳がない。
…あなたの常識に、そういう女はいるかしら？」
lines.english: “Otherwise, how could she go on loving a man she hadn’t seen in five years? Can your idea of what’s normal even account for a woman like that?”
“Ngh…”

lines.japanese:
「だから、これからも忘れない。
下手をしたら…いえ、今のままじゃ確実に、
一生、新しい恋なんてできるわけがない」
lines.english: “That is why she won’t forget you. If things go badly… no, as they stand now, she will never fall in love with anyone else for the rest of her life.”

lines.japanese:
「そんな、そんな…
俺なんて、ほんの一年間クラスメートだっただけで、
あいつにそんな想われることしたわけじゃ…」
lines.english: “No… I was only her classmate for a single year. I never did anything to deserve that kind of love from her…”

lines.japanese: 「それを決めるのは、あなたじゃなくてかずさよね？」
lines.english: “That is for Kazusa to decide, not you.”

lines.japanese: どうして親子そろって同じ事言うんだ…
lines.english: Why did mother and daughter both say exactly the same thing…?

lines.japanese:
これじゃまるで、曜子さんの言ってることが
全部かずさの気持ちそのものみたいじゃないか。
lines.english: It made every word from Youko sound as if it had come straight from Kazusa’s heart.

lines.japanese: 「もう一度言うわよ…北原春希くん」
lines.english: “I’ll say it once more, Haruki Kitahara.”

lines.japanese: けど、けど…曜子さん。
lines.english: But… Youko…

lines.japanese:
「あなたがあの子を受け入れられないのなら、
今すぐあの子を捨てて。
…それが、あの子の為なんだから」
lines.english: “If you cannot accept her, abandon her now. That is what’s best for her.”

lines.japanese:
そんなことをしたら、かずさは…
あいつは、どうなるんですか…？
lines.english: If I did that, what would happen to Kazusa? What would become of her?

lines.japanese:
俺だけじゃなく、曜子さんにすら
もう、頼れなくなってしまったら…
lines.english: If she could no longer depend on me—or even on Youko…

lines.japanese:
目指すべき頂が、たった一つの道標が、
まるで蜃気楼のように消えてしまったら…
lines.english: If the summit she had pursued, the only guidepost she possessed, vanished like a mirage…

lines.japanese: 誰が、あいつを守ってやれるんですか…？
lines.english: who would be left to protect her?

lines.japanese: 「………さん、北原さんってば」
lines.english: “…Mr. Kitahara? Mr. Kitahara!”

lines.japanese:
「っ！？
え？　あ、ああ、ごめん、何？」
lines.english: “What!? Oh—sorry. What is it?”

lines.japanese:
「…なんか疲れてるみたいだねって言ったんだけど、
もう答えは聞いたような気がするからいいや」
lines.english: “I said you looked tired. But I think I just got my answer, so never mind.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese:
ずっと考え事してたら、
いつの間にか夜になっていた。
lines.english: I had spent so long lost in thought that night had fallen without my noticing.

lines.japanese: 曜子さんのこと、かずさのこと、そして今夜の約束のこと。
lines.english: I had been thinking about Youko, Kazusa, and the plans I had made for tonight.

lines.japanese:
色んな考えが頭の中でごちゃごちゃに混ざり、
整理も決断もできないままかずさの部屋を訪れると、
玄関に一枚の紙が貼ってあるだけだった。
lines.english: All of it churned together in my head. Still unable to sort out my thoughts or make a decision, I went to Kazusa’s apartment and found only a sheet of paper taped to the door.

lines.japanese: 『美代子さんと打ち合わせ。夕食はいらない』
lines.english: “Meeting with Miyoko. Don’t need dinner.”

lines.japanese:
あれだけ激しい気持ちを露わにしておきながら、
肝心なところで気を使う、的外れな小心者…
lines.english: After baring feelings that intense, she chose the one moment when it mattered to be timid and considerate in all the wrong ways. What a hopeless coward…

lines.japanese:
「あまり箸も進んでないみたいだし、
もしかしたら具合が悪いんじゃない？
雪菜、ちょっとあれ持ってきてあれ」
lines.english: “You’ve hardly touched your food. Are you sure you aren’t coming down with something? Setsuna, bring me the thing—you know, that.”

lines.japanese: 「あれじゃなくて体温計ってちゃんと言ってよ」
lines.english: “It’s called a thermometer, Mom. You can just say so.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、いえ、気遣っていただかなくてもいいです。
別にそんな大したことじゃ…」
lines.english: “No, really, you don’t need to worry. It’s nothing serious.”

lines.japanese:
「………もしかして、
昨夜、姉ちゃんが寝かせてくれなかった？」
lines.english: “…Did my sister keep you up all night?”
“Pffft!?”

lines.japanese: 「孝宏！」
lines.english: “Takahiro!”

lines.japanese:
さっきまで喉を通らなかった食事が、
今度はハッキリと詰まってしまった。
lines.english: The food that had barely been going down before now lodged firmly in my throat.

lines.japanese:
「この子は…もうハタチになろうってのに、
まるで中学生みたいなことに興味持って…」
lines.english: “Honestly, that boy… He’ll be twenty soon, and he’s still fascinated by the same things as a middle-schooler.”

lines.japanese: 「よさないか…食事中だぞ」
lines.english: “That’s enough. We’re eating.”

lines.japanese:
「なんで食事中にふさわしくない話だってわかるのさ？
夜中じゅう、ずっとゲームに付き合わされてたのって、
そういうこと聞こうとしてたかもしんないじゃん俺」
lines.english: “Why’d you assume I meant something unfit for the dinner table? Maybe I was asking if she made him play video games with her all night.”

lines.japanese:
「しかも言い逃れまで中学生みたい。
そんなんで、彼女に逃げられても知らないわよ」
lines.english: “And his excuses are straight out of middle school too. Don’t come crying to me when your girlfriend leaves you.”

lines.japanese:
「ちょ、ちょっと待ってくれよ！
家に十回くらい連れてきただけで彼女かよ！？」
lines.english: “H-Hold on! I bring a girl home ten times and suddenly she’s my girlfriend?”

lines.japanese: 「紛れもなく彼女でしょ」
lines.english: “She quite obviously is.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、あの、全然そういうことじゃないですから！
ただちょっと考え事してただけで」
lines.english: “This really isn’t anything like that! I was only distracted by a few things.”

lines.japanese:
何がそういうことなのかはともかく、
この一家は時々そういうことを包み隠さず話して、
俺を思いっきり口ごもらせる。
lines.english: Whatever “that” was supposed to mean, this family sometimes discussed such things with complete candor and left me utterly tongue-tied.

lines.japanese:
…まぁ、逆にこういう一家だからこそ、
雪菜を大っぴらに部屋に泊めることもできるんだけど。
lines.english: Then again, it was precisely because they were this kind of family that Setsuna could openly spend the night at my apartment.

lines.japanese:
「考え事…ねぇ。
将来のこととか？」
lines.english: “Distracted, huh? Thinking about the future?”

lines.japanese: 「将来？」
lines.english: “The future?”

lines.japanese: 「っ…お、おい」
lines.english: “H-Hey now…”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと孝宏、それは…」
lines.english: “Takahiro, perhaps that’s…”

lines.japanese:
「何言ってんだよ。
さっきからみんな聞きたくてウズウズしてるくせに」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. You’ve all been dying to ask him since he walked in.”

lines.japanese: 「え、何を？」
lines.english: “Ask me what?”

lines.japanese: 「…ええと」
lines.english: “Well…”

lines.japanese:
何のことかと雪菜に目配せしたけれど、
それは完全に空振りに終わってしまった。
lines.english: I glanced at Setsuna for some hint of what they meant, but the appeal fell utterly flat.

lines.japanese:
何しろ、全員黙りこくってしまった小木曽家の中でも
雪菜が一番気まずそうに俯いてしまっていたから。
lines.english: Of everyone in the suddenly silent Ogiso household, she was the one staring down at the table with the greatest embarrassment.

lines.japanese:
「あのさ、北原さん。
もしかしてさ………姉ちゃんにプロポーズした？」
lines.english: “Listen, Mr. Kitahara… did you maybe propose to my sister?”

lines.japanese:
テーブルの上…
雪菜が右手で左手をそっと隠した。
lines.english: Across the table, Setsuna quietly covered her left hand with her right.

lines.japanese: …新しい指輪が燦然と輝くその薬指を。
lines.english: More precisely, the ring finger where her new ring gleamed.

lines.japanese:
「姉ちゃんに聞いてもハッキリ言わないしさ。
父さんなんか今週すっごい暗かったんだぜ？」
lines.english: “She won’t give me a straight answer. Dad’s been in a terrible mood all week, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「っ…いい加減なことを言うな！」
lines.english: “Don’t talk nonsense!”

lines.japanese:
そういえば…
指輪を渡して以来、初めての小木曽家だった。
lines.english: Come to think of it, this was my first visit to the Ogisos since giving Setsuna the ring.

lines.japanese:
「た、孝宏…
何もそんな…食事中に。
ほら北原さん困ってるじゃないの」
lines.english: “T-Takahiro, really… Must you bring this up at dinner? Look how uncomfortable you’re making Mr. Kitahara.”

lines.japanese:
「ああっ、今になって急に自分だけいい顔して～！
どうやって口を割らせようかって、
最初に相談持ちかけたのはそっちだろ！」
lines.english: “Now you’re trying to look innocent! You were the one who asked me how we could make him confess!”

lines.japanese:
「…ええと。
だからそういう身も蓋もないことを
食事中にバラさなくても、ねぇ？」
lines.english: “Well… You didn’t have to blurt out the whole unvarnished story over dinner, did you?”

lines.japanese:
毎日顔を合わせてて薬指の変化に気づかないほど、
絆の浅い家族じゃないってわかってたのに。
lines.english: I knew this family was too close-knit to see Setsuna every day and not notice a new ring on her finger.

lines.japanese:
指摘されるまで知らぬ顔を決め込むなんて、
皆にとっても、雪菜にとっても、
取っていい態度じゃなかったはずなのに。
lines.english: Pretending ignorance until they confronted us had been unfair to all of them—and unfair to Setsuna most of all.

lines.japanese:
「ちょ、ちょっと、やめてよ。
別にこれは、そんな深い意味は…」
lines.english: “C-Could we stop? It doesn’t mean anything that serious…”

lines.japanese:
「…ないの？
だってそれ、随分と高そうじゃない？
前のオモチャみたいな安っぽいのと全然違うし」
lines.english: “It doesn’t? But that ring looks awfully expensive. Nothing like that cheap little toy you wore before.”

lines.japanese: 「…すいません、安っぽくて」
lines.english: “…Sorry it was so cheap.”

lines.japanese: 「…前のも春希くんに貰ったものなんだけど」
lines.english: “Haruki gave me the old one too, Mom.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、あら…そ、そう。それはあれね…
ほら、あれよあれ、ねぇ孝宏」
lines.english: “Oh! I-I see. Well, that’s… you know. That thing. Isn’t it, Takahiro?”

lines.japanese:
「つまりさぁ、
姉ちゃんが前もってきっちり説明しとけば、
こうして北原さんに恥をかかせることもなかったと…」
lines.english: “Meaning that if she’d explained things properly in the first place, Mr. Kitahara wouldn’t have been embarrassed like this…”

lines.japanese:
「そ、それよそれ！
ほんとこの子ってば、
肝心なところで変に頑固なんだから」
lines.english: “Exactly! Honestly, Setsuna, you choose the strangest moments to be stubborn.”

lines.japanese:
「だ、だからぁ、違うんだってば。
別にこれは…今すぐって意味じゃないんだから」
lines.english: “I keep telling you, it isn’t like that. The ring doesn’t mean we’re getting married right away.”

lines.japanese: 「雪菜…その言い方だと」
lines.english: “Setsuna… when you put it that way…”

lines.japanese:
「だよねぇ春希くん？
わたしたち、そんな…ねぇ？」
lines.english: “That’s right, isn’t it, Haruki? We’re not… you know?”

lines.japanese: 「…春希くん？」
lines.english: “…Haruki?”

lines.japanese:
「ええと…
『今すぐ』ではないってことは…？」
lines.english: “So… if it doesn’t mean ‘right now’…”

lines.japanese:
「要するに…
『将来的には』って話があったってこと？」
lines.english: “Does that mean you two have talked about ‘someday’?”
“Ngh…”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 「あ～あ、語るに落ちちゃった…」
lines.english: “And there it is. She gave herself away.”
“What? How…?”

lines.japanese:
「ほ～ら孝宏！
やっぱりお母さんの言った通りだったでしょ！
絶対何かあるってピンと来たんだから！」
lines.english: “There, Takahiro! I told you I was right! I knew there had to be something behind it.”

lines.japanese:
「なんだよ母さん。
自分で聞けもしなかったくせに急に調子付いちゃって」
lines.english: “You couldn’t even ask them yourself, Mom. Don’t start celebrating now.”

lines.japanese:
「やめないかお前たち！
要するに何も決まってないってことだと言ってるだろ！」
lines.english: “That is enough! They’re telling us nothing has been decided!”

lines.japanese:
「いや言ってない。言ってないよ。
ほとんど決まったって言ってんだよ」
lines.english: “No, they aren’t. They’re telling us it’s practically settled.”

lines.japanese:
「お父さん…
いくら認めたくないからって、
あまりにも自分の都合のいいように聞き違えるのは…」
lines.english: “Dear… I know you don’t want to accept this, but that is an astonishingly convenient way to mishear them.”

lines.japanese:
「ちょ、ちょっとぉ！
だから、だからぁ…
本人の前でそういう話はやめてよぉ」
lines.english: “W-Wait! I told you, I told you… Please don’t discuss this in front of him!”
“Ha… ha-ha.”

lines.japanese: なのに俺は…
lines.english: And yet I…

lines.japanese:
この、軽くて浮き足立った雰囲気の中でも。
一世一代の決め所かもしれなかった場面でも…
lines.english: even amid that buoyant, giddy excitement—even at what might have been the defining moment of my life…

lines.japanese:
流れを掴むことも、流れを止めることもできず、
ただ、俯いて黙り込んでいるだけだった。
lines.english: could neither join in nor put a stop to it. I could only lower my eyes and say nothing.

lines.japanese:
深く、沈み込んだ気持ちのまま。
ただ、必死で作った笑顔だけを表情に貼りつかせて。
lines.english: My spirits had sunk. All I could do was desperately hold a manufactured smile in place.

lines.japanese:
「今日はごめんね…
なんか変な話になっちゃって」
lines.english: “I’m sorry about tonight. The conversation got so strange…”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そんなこと…」
lines.english: “No, it’s fine…”

lines.japanese: こっちこそ、ごめん。
lines.english: I was the one who owed her an apology.

lines.japanese:
「もう、みんな気が早すぎるんだから。
本人たちほったらかして勝手に盛り上がっちゃって…」
lines.english: “They’re all getting so far ahead of themselves. They left us out of it and worked themselves into a frenzy…”

lines.japanese: 「だから、気にしてないって」
lines.english: “I told you, it didn’t bother me.”

lines.japanese:
気が早すぎても、問題ないはずだった。
それどころか、正式に申し込むべき話の流れだった。
lines.english: It should not have mattered that they were getting ahead of themselves. If anything, it had been the perfect opening for me to make a formal proposal.

lines.japanese:
だって、気が早い『だけ』で、
言ってることは間違ってない…はずなんだから。
lines.english: They were only getting ahead of themselves. What they were saying wasn’t wrong… or at least, it shouldn’t have been.

lines.japanese:
だから、ごめん。
黙ってて、ごめん。
大事なこと、言えなくてごめん。
lines.english: So I’m sorry. Sorry I kept silent. Sorry I couldn’t say what mattered.

lines.japanese:
「本当にごめんなさい。
でも、お母さんも孝宏も悪気はないの。
お父さんは………後でちゃんと話しておくから」
lines.english: “I really am sorry. Mom and Takahiro didn’t mean any harm. As for Dad… I’ll have a proper talk with him later.”

lines.japanese: 「うん…」
lines.english: “All right…”

lines.japanese:
なのに、そんな俺の致命的なミスを、
雪菜は自分の落ち度のように、何度も謝る。
lines.english: Yet Setsuna kept apologizing for my fatal mistake as though it were her own.

lines.japanese:
俺に負担を掛けないように。
俺に責任を負わせないように。
lines.english: She was trying not to burden me. Trying not to impose responsibility on me.

lines.japanese:
自分が何を求めているのか、
俺にどうして欲しいのか…
lines.english: What she wanted—what she wanted me to do…

lines.japanese:
ほんの少しだけ気持ちが漏れ出たけれど、
それを失言と片づけて、
あとは全て自分の中に押し込んで。
lines.english: had escaped her for one brief moment. Then she dismissed it as a slip and forced everything else back down inside herself.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ…」
lines.english: “Well, then…”

lines.japanese: 「また来週…ね」
lines.english: “Next week… okay?”

lines.japanese:
「うん。
連絡する」
lines.english: “Yeah. I’ll call you.”

lines.japanese: 「ばいばい…」
lines.english: “Bye…”

lines.japanese:
小木曽家での夕餉は、いつも以上に盛り上がった。
…まぁ、うち一人は途中で席を立ってしまったけど。
lines.english: Dinner at the Ogisos had been livelier than ever, though one of us did leave the table partway through.
lines.japaneseRuby:
小木曽家での[R夕餉^ゆうげ]は、いつも以上に盛り上がった。
…まぁ、うち一人は途中で席を立ってしまったけど。

lines.japanese:
お母さんは、もう親戚の予定を気にしだして、
『内輪で』を多用する若手組と真っ向から対立し。
lines.english: Her mother had already begun worrying about the relatives’ schedules, clashing head-on with the younger contingent, who kept insisting it should be “just family.”

lines.japanese:
孝宏君は、雪菜が出ていった後の部屋の使用権を主張し、
『そのままにしておく』という女性組と真っ向から対立し。
lines.english: Takahiro claimed Setsuna’s room for himself once she moved out, provoking another head-on clash with the women, who wanted it “left exactly as it was.”

lines.japanese:
お父さんはそういう話には参加したがらなかったけれど、
去り際、俺の母親に一度会う必要があると呟いた。
lines.english: Her father kept out of the discussion, but as I left, he muttered that he would need to meet my mother at least once.

lines.japanese:
そんな、小木曽家では当然の…
北原家には存在しない、しがらみだらけの会話。
lines.english: It was the sort of conversation that came naturally to the Ogisos: a thicket of family ties unknown in the Kitahara home.

lines.japanese:
すこし辟易しつつ、少し羨望を抱き、
そして徐々に、自分も染まっていくはずだったのに。
lines.english: I was supposed to find it a little exhausting, envy it a little, and gradually let it color me too.

lines.japanese:
あの、温かくて大らかな輪の中に
望んで入っていくはずだったのに。
lines.english: I was supposed to step willingly into that warm, generous circle.

lines.japanese:
大阪まで追いかけて、
雪菜を抱きしめたのは…
lines.english: I had chased Setsuna all the way to Osaka and held her in my arms…

lines.japanese:
お互いの気持ちを確かめあったのは、
たった一週間前のことのはずなのに。
lines.english: It was only a week ago that we had confirmed how we felt about each other.

lines.japanese:
今はもう、
それからどのくらい時間が経ったのかもわからない。
lines.english: Now I could no longer tell how much time had passed since then.

lines.japanese:
決めたはずの心は、
もう迷わないと誓ったはずの愛は。
lines.english: I thought I had made up my mind. I thought I had sworn that my love would never waver again.

lines.japanese:
まるで何もかも忘れようとしているかのような、
激しい情欲のぶつけあいの果てに…
lines.english: After that desperate outpouring of passion, as though we were trying to forget everything…

lines.japanese:
真に俺たちが結びたかった絆を。
繋げたかった心を。
もしかして、あやふやなものにしてしまったんだろうか。
lines.english: had we perhaps left uncertain the bond we had truly meant to forge—the hearts we had truly meant to join?
